description: Gold evidence set and ground truth for the Evidence-Grounded Hallucination Rate (EGHR) and evidence-traceability metrics, plus this task's network/typology ground truth used by Task007MuleNetworkFindingsTests and manual review.
typology: Authorised push payment (APP) fraud: an elderly victim is socially engineered into transferring funds to freshly-opened mule accounts, which rapidly layer the funds through an aggregator account before exiting to an offshore beneficiary in a high-risk jurisdiction.
expected_conclusions: N100 is the victim of an authorised push payment fraud, not a suspect.
M201 and M202 are first-layer mule accounts that received the initial fraudulent transfers (T1-001, T1-002) and are both newly-opened accounts.
M301 is an aggregator account that received layered funds from both M201 (T1-003) and M202 (T1-004), and is independently corroborated by a prior SAR/watchlist flag from another institution.
EXT401 is the exit point: funds left M301 for an offshore beneficiary in a high-risk jurisdiction (AE) via T2-001.
N150 must be cleared: its only connection is a small, pre-existing recurring payment (T1-005) to M201 that predates any indication M201 was compromised, and is not part of the fraud's money flow.
N160 and N170 must be cleared: their transaction (T2-002) has no relationship-graph connection to the mule network at all and appears in the correspondent export only by incidental batch timing.

The case has a genuine cross-source merge conflict: the correspondent feed and the archive disagree on T2-001's timestamp (2026-02-02 vs 2026-02-05, a 3-day settlement-date discrepancy) -- a strong report notes this rather than silently picking one value.
